title: Legora Launches Agentic Operating System for Legal Work
summary: Legora unveils AI-powered operating system using OpenAI models to automate legal workflows, contract analysis, and research. See how it transforms legal work.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- Legora launched an agentic operating system that automates contract review, legal research, and document drafting using OpenAI models.
- The platform integrates ChatGPT and Codex to handle routine legal tasks, freeing lawyers for strategic client work.
- Law firms using Legora report 60% faster contract analysis and significant reductions in manual document processing time.


Legora has introduced an agentic operating system designed to transform how legal professionals handle contracts, research, and document workflows. Officially launched on October 28, 2026, the platform leverages OpenAI's models including ChatGPT and Codex to automate routine legal tasks and accelerate case preparation. The system represents a shift from single-task AI tools to a comprehensive operating environment where autonomous agents collaborate on complex legal workflows.


## How the Agentic System Works


Legora's platform deploys specialized AI agents that handle distinct aspects of legal work. Contract review agents scan agreements for risk clauses, compliance gaps, and non-standard terms. Research agents query case law databases and synthesize relevant precedents. Document drafting agents generate first drafts of briefs, motions, and correspondence based on attorney guidance. These agents operate within an[agentic workflow](https://emergent.sh/glossary/agentic-workflow) framework, passing tasks between specialized modules and escalating complex decisions to human lawyers.


The system integrates directly with existing legal software ecosystems, pulling data from case management platforms and document repositories. Attorneys interact through a unified interface that surfaces agent recommendations, flags high-priority items, and provides audit trails for every automated action. OpenAI's Codex powers the system's ability to understand legal code structures and automate repetitive coding tasks within legal tech stacks.


## Contract Analysis at Scale


One of Legora's core capabilities is contract analysis. The platform can process hundreds of agreements simultaneously, identifying clauses that deviate from firm standards or client preferences. Early adopters report 60% faster contract turnaround times compared to manual review processes. The system highlights liability exposure, payment terms, and termination conditions, generating summary memos that attorneys can review in minutes rather than hours.


- Automated extraction of key terms, dates, and parties from complex agreements
- Risk scoring based on firm-specific criteria and industry benchmarks
- Clause libraries that suggest standard language for common contract sections
- Version tracking that flags changes across multiple contract drafts


## Legal Research Acceleration


Legora's research agents combine ChatGPT's natural language understanding with legal databases to answer complex queries. Attorneys can ask conversational questions like "Find appellate cases in the Ninth Circuit addressing trade secret misappropriation in the SaaS context since 2024" and receive annotated results with case summaries and relevance scores. The system continuously learns from attorney feedback, refining its understanding of what constitutes a strong precedent for specific practice areas.


The platform also monitors regulatory changes and alerts attorneys when new statutes or rulings affect active cases. This proactive monitoring reduces the risk of missing critical legal developments that could impact client strategy.


## Release Date and Availability


Legora officially released its agentic operating system on October 28, 2026, following beta testing with mid-sized law firms and corporate legal departments. The platform is currently available through enterprise licensing agreements, with pricing based on the number of attorneys and transaction volume. OpenAI's blog post announcing the launch emphasizes the collaboration between Legora's legal domain experts and OpenAI's AI research teams in developing the system's specialized capabilities.


## What This Means for Legal Practice


Legora's launch signals a maturation of AI in legal work, moving beyond simple document search to autonomous task execution. By handling routine contract review, research synthesis, and drafting tasks, the platform enables lawyers to focus on client counseling, negotiation strategy, and courtroom advocacy. The agentic approach, where multiple AI agents collaborate on complex workflows, offers a blueprint for how professional services firms can integrate AI without replacing human expertise. As legal AI adoption accelerates, platforms like Legora are likely to become standard infrastructure in modern law firms.
